title: noc_panel_rows undercounts drawn rows by 3 (header/drops/crisis sections), so max scroll can never reach the drop-log tail
evidence:
measure (noc_panel_rows):
	rows := i32(2) // header: title + global line
	rows += 2      // drops
	rows += 2      // crisis root causes
	rows += 1      // rejections
draw (draw_noc_panel) emits 3 header rows:
	cur = noc_row(v, cur, scroll, visible, "DEBUG OVERLAY (D)", NOC_INK)
	cur = noc_row(v, cur, scroll, visible, glob, NOC_INK_DIM)
	hash := fmt.tprintf("hash %016x", stats.sim_hash)
	cur = noc_row(v, cur, scroll, visible, hash, NOC_INK_SOFT)
3 drop rows ("DROPS since start...", drops_line, ratio_line) and 4 crisis/rej rows ("CRISIS root causes", sat row, pool_line, rej). Clamp at :435:
	scroll := clamp(scroll_in, 0, max(0, total - visible))
detail: Draw emits 10 rows where the measure counts 7 (header 3vs2, drops 3vs2, crisis+rej 4vs3). visible=50; scroll max = total-visible, so the last 3 content rows (oldest drop-log rows) are permanently unreachable.
recommended_fix: Count 3 header rows (include the hash line), 3 drop rows, and 4 crisis/rejection rows in noc_panel_rows so the measure matches the draw.

title: Measure/draw drift on conditional rows: empty-state placeholders uncounted; selected-pipe readout counted as 4 but draws 0-4
detail: Empty events/log states draw 2 extra unmeasured rows; a dead or stats-less selected pipe draws 0-1 rows vs 4 measured (per-class also skips out-of-roster classes without counting). Scroll range is wrong in these states.
recommended_fix: Mirror the draw predicates exactly in noc_panel_rows: +1 per placeholder when empty, sel-pipe rows only when pipe_slot succeeds and a stats row exists, count only in-roster classes.

title: overlay-check T1 sidecar skips paused-tick hashes while the blessed golden emits one per wall tick — diverges for paused demos
detail: The blessed goldens/<demo>.t1 contains one hash per wall tick including paused ticks; the sidecar omits them. For demos with pauses in [1,cap_ms] (demos/pause.dem has a 190-tick window) the streams misalign — the AC3 byte-compare fails.
recommended_fix: In overlay_check's paused branch, append the stable state_hash (mirroring run_demo) instead of `continue`, keeping sidecar and golden tick-for-tick identical.

title: tools/run-dev.sh collects extra CLI args but never forwards them to the app; "${ARGS[@]+}" passes a single empty-string arg to odin build
evidence:
# tools/run-dev.sh --stats-out

# pass-through (the app's telemetry flag) ... odin build app -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:bin/app-dev "${ARGS[@]+}" 2>&1 | head -20 ... PP_NOC_E2E=1 ./bin/app-dev ... ./bin/app-dev (bash-verified: with ARGS=(--stats-out foo), "${ARGS[@]+}" expands to exactly ONE empty-string word)
detail: ARGS never reach ./bin/app-dev (invoked bare in both branches), and a non-empty ARGS injects an empty-string argument into the odin build command. The documented --stats-out pass-through silently does nothing.
recommended_fix: Use "${ARGS[@]+"${ARGS[@]}"}" on the build line (or drop build args) and run "./bin/app-dev "${ARGS[@]+"${ARGS[@]}"}" so pass-through args reach the app.

title: Rejection latch dedups on (sim tick, kind): two same-kind rejections within one 20Hz tick count once
evidence:
if app.input.last_reject != .None && (app.input.reject_tick != app.noc_reject_tick || app.input.last_reject != app.noc_reject_kind) {
				rnd.noc_feed_reject(&app.noc_feed, app.input.last_reject)
exec (per rejection):
		inp.last_reject = err
		inp.reject_tick = inp.tick
ictx.tick = app.tick (main.odin:753) — the sim tick, advanced at 20Hz while input runs at 60fps
detail: reject_tick is the sim tick; input frames run ~3x per tick. A repeated same-kind invalid edit within one tick (~50ms, e.g. rapid double-click) is not counted — REJECTED total undercounts.
recommended_fix: Latch on a monotonically changing witness (e.g. a per-rejection sequence counter or frame index) instead of (tick, kind), so every distinct rejection event counts.

title: Drop-log rows resolve stale bundle slots against the CURRENT bundle table — an occupied renumbered slot shows the wrong pipe/endpoints/lane
detail: Bundle slots renumber on every rebuild. An in-range stale slot whose index now belongs to a different live bundle matches that bundle's pipe and prints its bundle_lo/hi and lane — misanchored, not "gone"; the stated guard only covers unoccupied/out-of-range slots.
recommended_fix: Store the drop-time bundle identity (e.g. the lo/hi node pair) in Drop_Log_Entry and compare against the resolved bundle's pair, rendering "gone" on mismatch.
